distinguishing_features: Infuses a hydrophobic lubricant into evaporator tube surfaces (SLIPS-type slippery liquid-infused interface) to prevent adhesion, whereas PRIOR ART 3 uses chemical antiscalant dosing plus a temperature setpoint reduction.
Addresses scale adhesion at the surface/lubricant interface via reduced adhesion energy rather than sequestering or altering bulk supersaturation chemistry.
Relies on a porous ceramic plus silicone (PDMS) coating system rather than a chemical treatment loop.
Keeps the monitoring role of pH/conductivity purely as supplemental correlation, not as a dosing gate.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Prevent scale from adhering to and fouling evaporator tube surfaces so heat transfer and evaporation rate are not degraded.
parsed.viable_reason: The silicone/PDMS lubricant would be shear-depleted and washed out by the high-solids black-liquor flow, and the physics check is internally inconsistent (0.005 Pa shear stress cannot exceed a ~10 J/m2 adhesion energy, and 'self-replenishing via liquor flow' is implausible), so the mechanism is not feasible as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: A slippery liquid-infused hydrophobic surface to defeat scale adhesion is a distinct surface-engineering mechanism, not a routine parameter change of the antiscalant-dosing or monitoring prior art.
